text.en: In imperative sentences, the sentence-final portion tends to be pronounced longer and more emphatically than in declarative sentences. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sato-imperative-lengthened-emphasis⟧
text.ja: 命令文では、平叙文よりも文末がやや長く強めに発音される傾向がある。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sato-imperative-lengthened-emphasis⟧

text.en: In the Tokachi dialect, a non-rising intonation contour occurs in interrogatives that lack a final predicate verb and end in a noun, nominalizer, or conjunctive particle followed by an interrogative particle. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--tokachi-interrogative-non-rising-conditions⟧
text.ja: 十勝方言では、文末述語動詞を欠き、名詞・形式名詞または接続小詞に疑問小詞が後続する形で終わる疑問文において、非上昇イントネーションが生じる。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--tokachi-interrogative-non-rising-conditions⟧

text.en: Declarative intonation varies across dialects. In Sakhalin Ainu, declarative sentences are generally pronounced with rising intonation, while interrogative sentences are pronounced with falling intonation. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-declarative-rising-interrogative-falling⟧ In the Shizunai dialect, by contrast, sentence intonation is slightly falling in declarative sentences. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-declarative-falling-intonation⟧ In the Saru dialect, pitch in ordinary declarative speech exhibits a natural decline without a final rise or fall at the end of the sentence. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-declarative-natural-pitch-decline⟧ More broadly, affirmative sentences tend to show a slight sentence-final rise, though not as high as in interrogative sentences. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--ainu-affirmative-slight-final-rise⟧ In the Saru dialect, a rising intonation contour additionally appears when the speaker expects a reaction from the interlocutor. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-rising-contour-reaction-expectation⟧
text.ja: 平叙文のイントネーションは方言によって異なる。樺太アイヌ語では、叙述文が一般的に上昇音調で発話され、疑問文は下降音調で発話される。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-declarative-rising-interrogative-falling⟧ これに対し、静内方言では平叙文の文イントネーションがわずかに下降する。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-declarative-falling-intonation⟧ 沙流方言の通常の平叙発話では、文末の上昇や下降を伴わず自然にピッチが下降する。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-declarative-natural-pitch-decline⟧ より広く見ると、肯定文では文末のイントネーションがやや上がり気味になる傾向があるが、疑問文ほどは上昇しない。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--ainu-affirmative-slight-final-rise⟧ さらに沙流方言では、聞き手からの反応を期待する場合に上昇イントネーションが現れる。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-rising-contour-reaction-expectation⟧

text.en: Interrogative intonation also differs across dialects. In the Shizunai dialect, sentence intonation rises gradually in questions. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-interrogative-rising-intonation⟧ In that same dialect, the use of sentence-final particles and forms greatly diminishes the importance of intonation. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-particles-diminish-intonation-importance⟧ In the Saru dialect, interrogative pitch movement and intensity peaks occur primarily on sentence-final interrogative particles such as *hawe*, *ya*, *a*, and *he*. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-interrogative-pitch-peak-final-particle⟧ Interrogative sentences without a final rising pitch contour are attested in the Saru dialect. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-interrogative-non-rising-contour-attested⟧ More specifically, interrogative sentences ending in *nankora* in acoustic data of the Saru dialect are uttered with a falling intonation contour. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-nankora-falling-intonation⟧ In Sakhalin Ainu, sentences ending in the final particle *hVV* take falling intonation in questions and rising intonation in non-questions. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-hvv-falling-question-rising-non-question⟧
text.ja: 疑問文のイントネーションも方言によって異なる。静内方言では、疑問文の文イントネーションが次第に上昇する。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-interrogative-rising-intonation⟧ 同方言において、文末小詞や文末形式の使用によりイントネーションの重要性は大幅に減少している。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--shizunai-particles-diminish-intonation-importance⟧ 沙流方言では、疑問文のピッチ変動と強度のピークが主に文末の疑問小詞（*hawe*・*ya*・*a*・*he*）に現れる。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-interrogative-pitch-peak-final-particle⟧ 沙流方言において、文末上昇音調を伴わない疑問文の存在が確認されている。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-interrogative-non-rising-contour-attested⟧ より具体的には、沙流方言の音声データにおいて*nankora*で終わる疑問文は下降イントネーションで発話される。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-nankora-falling-intonation⟧ 樺太アイヌ語では、終助詞*hVV*を伴う文が疑問文で下降イントネーション、非疑問文で上昇イントネーションをとる。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-hvv-falling-question-rising-non-question⟧

text.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, utterances expressing surprise are typically spoken with falling intonation. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-surprise-falling-intonation⟧ In the Saru dialect, expressing exclamation or wish raises the pitch of the whole utterance and produces a lengthened rising-falling contour at the end of the sentence. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-exclamation-wish-rising-falling-contour⟧
text.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、驚きを表現する発話では下降音調が典型的である。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--sakhalin-surprise-falling-intonation⟧ 沙流方言では、感嘆や願望を表す際に発話全体のピッチが高くなり、文末に長引く上昇下降の音調が現れる。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--saru-exclamation-wish-rising-falling-contour⟧

text.en: In Hokkaido Ainu, a level or falling intonation contour implies continuation, whereas a rising contour marks utterance finality. ⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--hokkaido-continuation-falling-final-rising⟧
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語において、平坦または下降音調は後続発話の存在を暗示し、上昇音調は発話の終末を標示する。⟦claim:prosody/phrasal-and-utterance-intonation--hokkaido-continuation-falling-final-rising⟧
